claims.claim: Animal, object, interaction and instruction dimensions do not use SVG identifiers, classes, comments, metadata or invisible elements as evidence.
defeaters: A visual judge could still be manipulated by rendered prompt injection.
Human alignment has not yet been established.
The bridge study currently covers fixture renderings rather than the full prospective corpus.
claims.title: Semantic scores are source-independent

claims.claim: Repeated stochastic generations of the same semantic task remain identifiable as replicates rather than independent benchmark items.
defeaters: Provider-side unreported sampling state can remain unknown.
claims.title: Scenario, prompt, condition, trial and evaluation identities are distinct

claims.claim: V1 pilot scenarios are stratified by support, containment, control and propulsion interfaces rather than sampled as an arbitrary animal-object cross-product.
defeaters: Empirical item difficulty and coverage have not yet been measured.
claims.title: The prospective task set tests distinct mobility affordances

claims.claim: A run records tasks, trials, artifacts, canonical renders, evaluations, provenance and reproduction instructions using stable hashes.
defeaters: No independent remote reproduction has yet occurred.
claims.title: Runs are content-addressed and research-object ready

claims.claim: The analysis separates model, animal, object, relation and replicate effects and reports uncertainty rather than only point ranks.
defeaters: The estimator has not yet been fitted to a real prospective benchmark run.
claims.title: Uncertainty respects task and replicate structure

claims.claim: Automatic recognition, anatomy, mechanics and interaction scores are calibrated against blinded human assessment.
defeaters: No participant data have been collected.
claims.title: Automatic scores align with blinded human judgements

claims.claim: The benchmark records permissions and limits distribution of third-party text, images and annotations to permitted uses.
defeaters: Historical permissions and participant governance remain unresolved.
claims.title: Historical and participant data are rights-aware

claims.claim: The parser rejects active content, external resources and known complexity hazards before rendering or scoring.
defeaters: Coverage-guided fuzzing and independent security review have not yet occurred.
claims.title: Untrusted SVG source is bounded and adversarially tested

claims.claim: Calibration artifacts are selected reproducibly across interface, model, score-boundary and judge-disagreement strata, then presented in blinded within-task cross-model pairs.
defeaters: The design has not yet been used to recruit participants or collect ratings.
claims.title: Human calibration selection and presentation are prespecified

claims.claim: Animal, mobile-object, and interface ontologies expose JSON-LD, SHACL, and competency-test surfaces while external ontologies remain explicit references or reviewed mappings and the w3id namespace is not represented as published without resolver evidence.
defeaters: The w3id resolver has not yet been registered or independently verified.
The current SHACL and competency suite is an evaluation-ontology prototype rather than a mature community ontology.
No external semantic mapping has yet completed licence, version, and competency review.
claims.title: Ontology interoperability is formal, bounded, and namespace-honest

claims.claim: Direct, pattern-only, candidate, watch and excluded first-party assets are recorded with versioned contracts and checked evidence paths.
defeaters: The audit cannot prove optional sibling clones or external commands work when they are absent.
The owner ecosystem can change after the dated inventory snapshot.
claims.title: First-party ecosystem integration is explicit and auditable

claims.claim: Dylan Mordaunt's Hugging Face adapters are represented by immutable-revision, licence, runtime-profile and canary gates rather than presumed eligible.
defeaters: The first-party adapters have not yet completed an SVG canary or prospective run.
Hosted-provider behaviour is unavailable for adapters without deployed inference.
claims.title: First-party models use the ordinary qualification gates

claims.claim: The project can generate a deterministic content-addressed bundle for SourceRight, Authentext, scholarly review, Substack, approval-gated Postiz distribution, OSF and arXiv without performing authenticated external writes.
defeaters: The hand-offs have not yet executed against every external tool in a clean integration environment.
Publication claims still require human evidence review.
claims.title: Publication hand-offs are rights-aware and non-autonomous

claims.claim: The V1 exchange exports blinded categorical assignments, rejects direct-identifier columns and records a data dictionary and manifest.
defeaters: Collection platforms can still gather identifiers outside the released PelicanBench table.
Governance and consent have not yet been approved or tested with participants.
claims.title: Human-rating exchange minimises participant data

claims.claim: The 113-prompt candidate, its 81 semantic scenarios, three panels, nine canaries, empirical bridge and commitment are regenerated and validated fail-closed.
defeaters: The candidate has not yet been run against the prospective model panel.
claims.title: The prospective candidate is content-addressed and factorially checked

claims.claim: A deterministic rule-based annotation layer exactly reconstructs the 48 source prompts and verifies animal, mobile-object and relation coverage without presenting itself as a validated general NER model.
defeaters: The complete Simon archive still requires rights clearance and a manually annotated gold corpus.
claims.title: The empirical prompt bridge is auditable and source-derived

claims.claim: Model and judge canary plans are deterministic; missing or failed cells remain in denominators; judge technical qualification cannot be promoted to E3 without human agreement evidence.
defeaters: No live model or judge endpoint has completed qualification.
claims.title: Model and judge qualification retain failures and separate technical from empirical gates

claims.claim: Blind recognition is locked before prompt disclosure; direct identifiers are rejected; responses receive content-addressed chained receipts; transparent calibration summaries are executable.
defeaters: The reference interface is not an approved participant platform and no participants have been recruited.
claims.title: Human calibration is stage-gated and privacy-minimised

claims.claim: Repository-native syntax, AST, configuration, prose, contract, taxonomy, mutation-smoke and deterministic simulation gates run locally while unavailable external tools are explicitly deferred to fail-closed CI jobs.
defeaters: Ruff, mypy, Pyright, Vale, Hypothesis and full mutmut still require execution in an environment where they are installed.
claims.title: Quality gates remain executable when optional static-analysis tools are absent

v0.2-alpha.description: A locally fixture-verified measurement-validity alpha. It makes no empirical human-validity or production-hardening claim.

v0.3-alpha.description: A fixture-verified ecosystem, model-qualification and publication-integration alpha. It adds no empirical model or human-validity claim.

v0.4-alpha.description: A fixture-verified prospective-pilot and dependency-resilient quality alpha. It does not claim live model, judge, or participant calibration.

v1.0.description: The first empirically calibrated and reproducible public benchmark release.
